content.jointProblem: Can Bayesian state-space or recurrent models built from DataBridge AVL and timetable histories produce PassengerView ETAs within 90 seconds of actual arrival at least 85% of the time? A first experiment would test transfer to the Romanian networks using time-ordered historical replay, comparing the current timetable-offset baseline with locally calibrated models and separately evaluating peak-hour and disruption performance.

rationale.text: Novaković has directly relevant experience estimating bus travel times from archived AVL using state-space models, including uncertainty estimation.

sources.quote: This study develops a Kalman filter formulation that treats segment-level travel time as a latent state evolving according to a random-walk process
The filter's uncertainty estimates align well with empirical variance, making them suitable for downstream reliability analyses.

rationale.text: Her research includes recurrent models for the specific task of predicting arrivals at upcoming bus stops.

sources.quote: Long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks are evaluated for predicting bus arrival times at individual stops 1 to 5 stops ahead

rationale.text: Her AVL preprocessing work offers a concrete starting point for turning the company's largely unused archive into training data.

sources.quote: The pipeline consists of six sequential stages: deduplication, map matching, speed filtering, stop-event reconstruction, trip identification, and running-time segmentation.
Code is provided as open-source Python modules.

rationale.text: She has investigated cross-network transfer, providing relevant methods and evidence of limitations for adapting models to the Romanian customers.

sources.quote: Results suggest that transfer is beneficial when target-city data are scarce but that network topology differences limit gains beyond approximately 8 weeks of fine-tuning data.

rationale.text: Her current project addresses resource-constrained deployment, although its planned pilots are not evidence of validated production performance.

sources.quote: The project develops lightweight Bayesian and neural network models that can be retrained nightly on a standard server
Pilot deployments are planned in Novi Sad and one partner city.

rationale.text: A joint project matches her stated willingness to collaborate with companies operating urban mobility software.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies operating urban mobility platforms or fleet management software

constraints.text: Acceptance must use the contractual absolute arrival-error target, rather than treating published MAE, RMSE or MAPE results as equivalent evidence.

sources.quote: their contracts require displayed ETAs to be within 90 seconds of the bus's actual arrival at least 85 percent of the time.

constraints.text: Data access requires a signed agreement, and preprocessing must accommodate the archive's scale. Weather-dependent methods cannot assume an existing weather feed.

sources.quote: with access to our full historical AVL dataset and timetable logs under a signed data-sharing agreement.
The raw data sits in a PostgreSQL time-series table — roughly 2.8 billion rows at this point
We do not have weather data integrated yet.

constraints.text: Deployment and handover must fit the company's Java/on-premise environment and limited dedicated engineering capacity; a research prototype alone is insufficient.

sources.quote: Java 17 backend with Spring Boot microservices
Docker and Kubernetes on on-premise cluster in Subotica data centre
We can dedicate one senior backend engineer and one domain specialist part-time to a collaborative project
We have one data engineer on staff who knows Python well but has no background in time-series modelling.

constraints.text: The implementation schedule must be reconciled before committing: the company's stated approval expectation predates the researcher's stated capacity for one new collaboration in 2026.

sources.quote: The Romanian contracts have a twelve-month implementation window starting from go-live approval, which we expect in Q3 2024.
Workload is moderate; she can take on one new collaboration in 2026.

constraints.text: The data-sharing and publication terms must address her preference to publish anonymised results.

sources.quote: She prefers collaborations where her group retains the right to publish anonymised results.
under a signed data-sharing agreement.

risks: The stated implementation window may already be incompatible with the researcher's 2026 capacity. Actual approval dates and current researcher availability remain unconfirmed.

Published results concern other networks, sampling frequencies and evaluation metrics. They do not establish the Romanian contractual hit rate; the first replay experiment must explicitly test this transfer gap.

It is unknown how much of the historical archive covers each Romanian customer, whether stop events provide reliable arrival labels, or whether timetable versions can be reconstructed without leakage.
The published preprocessing pipeline was tested on much smaller archives than 2.8 billion rows; extraction and processing costs may dominate the initial work.

Her recurrent models underperformed on congested shared corridors, and her extreme-weather study found degraded early-event coverage. Missing weather integration and uncertain disruption labels may leave the most important failures unresolved.

Research-project plans for lightweight models do not demonstrate production serving, telemetry freshness or PassengerView integration at this company's scale. Available compute, operating budget and end-to-end latency limits are unknown.
Publication preferences may conflict with customer data restrictions unless anonymisation, permitted outputs and review procedures are agreed.
questions: What is the actual go-live approval date and remaining contractual window? Can Novaković confirm her current availability, start date and effort within the one-collaboration capacity noted for 2026?
How is the 85% target calculated: prediction horizons, eligible stops, aggregation by municipality, treatment of cancellations and stale displays, and definition of actual arrival?
Which Romanian networks are represented in the archive, for how long, and with what route shapes, historical timetable versions, trip identifiers and reliable door-event labels?

Can the initial experiment use a representative time-ordered holdout from each customer, with only information available at prediction time, to compare the current baseline, state-space and GRU approaches against the contractual hit rate?
What weather, roadworks and incident information can be obtained, and can peak-hour and disruption cases be evaluated separately before a live pilot?
What compute, memory, storage, inference latency and refresh-rate limits apply, and who will own Java integration, monitoring, retraining and fallback operation?
What project budget and staff effort are committed, and will the company support a staged data audit, replay evaluation and shadow deployment before acceptance testing?
Can all relevant operators authorise the data-sharing agreement, and what anonymisation, publication review, software ownership and customer-data segregation terms are required?
